tasks.short: Find prospective service customers from directories, referrals and events.

steps.what: Review territory, target criteria and existing accounts in the {CRM}.
Search business directories and collect relevant business details.
Discuss introductions and potential needs with clients or event contacts.
Combine leads in a {SPREADSHEET} and check existing records in the {CRM}.
Assess business fit and choose leads worth pursuing.

loop.input: Deduplicated lead records, source excerpts, referral notes and approved target criteria.
loop.output: Suggested fit category, supporting excerpts and unresolved questions for each lead.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; the seller confirms the shortlist.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair attempt per lead; incomplete or unsupported cases return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Industry and size filters are rules; referral language and service needs require contextual interpretation.

steps.what: Create or update lead records and assign the next action in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Approved directory feeds enter the {CRM} through a deterministic integration that checks identifiers and existing accounts, removing the separate {SPREADSHEET}. A bounded model loop interprets referral notes and proposes a sourced shortlist for seller review. Configured {CRM} rules assign approved leads and next actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directory access, inconsistent identifiers and referral notes made a reliable import expensive to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Integration code is cheaper to build, while a bounded classification loop can handle free-text referrals.
tasks.still_hard: Directory licences, stale contacts, ambiguous account matches and introductions that depend on personal trust.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a credible introduction and judging whether a service need is real.

ambition.what: Daily selection of the next prospect cohort within the assigned territory

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time assembling lists and more time testing prospect groups and developing introductions. They can reprioritise within their assigned territory; budget and territory rights need explicit delegation.

reach.task: Compare prospect cohorts and recommend changes to territory priorities.
reach.learn: Conversion analysis, sample size limits and selection bias.

evidence.claim: Lead research and fit assessment are supported by an existing sales qualification product.
Feed imports, duplicate checks and routing can use deterministic rules; referral interpretation can use a bounded loop.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The pilot covers one sales team, one {CRM} and approved directory sources.
The business directory is the OTHER category in step s2 and provides a licensed feed or export.
Referral discussions remain human; the solution does not contact prospects.
The {CRM} becomes the shared lead register, replacing the intermediate {SPREADSHEET}.
GDPR applies to identifiable contacts. Access planning includes lawful sourcing, retention and consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Available directory licences, feeds and export rights.
Actual lead volumes, duplicate rates and contact-data quality.
Whether the team currently maintains a separate lead workbook.
Approved target criteria and the seller's delegated prioritisation rights.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which available directory interfaces provide stable business identifiers and permitted reuse?
Can a sample of referral notes be classified accurately using the existing target criteria?
new_work: Review suggested fit categories and uncertain account matches.
Resolve failed imports and stale contact records.
Maintain source permissions, target criteria and duplicate rules.
Sample rejected leads to detect missed prospect groups.

tasks.short: Explain purchased service terms, contractual obligations and practical next steps to customers.

steps.what: Find the customer's signed contract and service record.
Read applicable clauses and identify dates, obligations and service limits.

loop.input: Authoritative signed contract, amendments, service record and the customer's question.
loop.output: Relevant obligations, dates and limits with clause references and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Check document version, source references and date formats; the seller verifies material facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; conflicting clauses or missing amendments go to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiated clauses and amendments cannot all be mapped reliably from fixed fields.

steps.what: Compose the customer explanation using approved wording.
Check recipient, terms and attachments, then send the explanation.
Discuss questions, explain consequences and resolve misunderstandings with the customer.
Log correspondence and follow-up actions in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A deterministic link joins the account in the {CRM} to authoritative contracts in the {CLM} and {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares cited facts for review, then configured templates produce the explanation in {EMAIL}; the seller approves each personalised send. Correspondence and confirmed follow-up actions are logged in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signed versions, amendments and service details were scattered, making reliable explanations depend on manual reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Document retrieval, source-linked extraction and template generation can now be combined at a practical implementation cost.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting amendments, disputed meanings and explaining unwelcome obligations without damaging trust.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding the customer's concern and explaining consequences without making unsupported promises.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time locating clauses and composing routine explanations. More time goes to difficult conversations; contractual authority does not change.

reach.task: Check that service handover instructions match the accepted contract.
reach.learn: Order fields, contract precedence and operational acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: An existing product combines customer records, quotes and online signing with approval-controlled AI actions.
Source-linked contract extraction and template generation are feasible design patterns; this workflow has no documented outcome in the digest.
A documented chatbot case illustrates the consequences of sending incorrect contractual information.
Time reductions and build ranges are estimates requiring a local pilot.

assumptions: The pilot covers one service family and a limited set of explanation templates.
Signed contracts and amendments have identifiable authoritative versions.
Configured templates cover routine explanations; unusual wording returns to the seller.
The workflow explains existing terms and does not amend contracts.
Logging uses sent messages and seller-confirmed notes, without introducing call recording.
GDPR requires account-level access and appropriate retention. Access estimates include consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Where authoritative signed versions and amendments are stored.
Which explanations require legal or service-delivery approval.
Whether contractual notice channels differ from ordinary customer email.
Existing document permissions, retention rules and integration access.
Applicable national consultation requirements and approval lead times.
research_questions: Can the retrieval process consistently identify the controlling contract and amendments?
Which common questions can be answered entirely through approved templates?
new_work: Verify extracted facts and approve personalised sends.
Resolve conflicting versions and ambiguous obligations.
Maintain templates, clause mappings and document permissions.
Sample explanations for unsupported statements and omitted limitations.
Route contractual disputes to the authorised role.

tasks.short: Recommend service features that match customer needs and delivery capabilities.

steps.what: Review account history and earlier requirements in the {CRM}.
Explore customer needs, priorities, constraints and acceptable trade-offs.
Check service descriptions, exclusions and delivery limits in approved documents.
Compare relevant features and prepare reasons for recommending each option.

loop.input: Confirmed customer requirements, rule-filtered services and approved capability descriptions.
loop.output: A comparison linking features and limitations to stated needs, with source references.
loop.check: Every service must pass eligibility rules; every capability claim needs an approved source; the seller reviews trade-offs.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported capabilities or conflicting requirements return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but linking conversational needs to feature explanations requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Recommend features, explain limitations and test the customer's understanding.
Record the recommendation and agreed next action in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A configured account view in the {CRM} provides history, while deterministic filters retrieve suitable services and their limitations from approved information in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a sourced comparison for the seller's conversation. The seller makes the recommendation and confirms structured requirements and next actions in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service knowledge was spread across documents, and recommendations depended on interpreting each customer's priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable capability records and inexpensive comparison generators reduce preparation without requiring automated recommendations.
tasks.still_hard: Discovering unstated needs, checking unusual delivery promises and balancing conflicting customer priorities.
tasks.human_edge: Eliciting priorities, challenging assumptions and accepting responsibility for the recommendation.

ambition.what: A documented service-fit review before renewal

tasks.altitude: The seller's week still centres on discovery and recommendation conversations, with shorter preparation and recording. They can propose service-fit reviews; authority to promise exceptions remains unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an initial feasibility brief for unusual service requirements.
reach.learn: Capability boundaries, requirement traceability and when specialist validation is needed.

evidence.claim: Rules can filter service options, while sourced drafting can reduce comparison preparation; the recommendation remains human.
Existing sales software supports customer records and approval-controlled assistance, but this does not establish recommendation quality.
Most conversation time remains because discovery and trade-off judgement dominate this task.

assumptions: The pilot covers ordinary services outside the excluded advertising, insurance, financial and travel categories.
Core eligibility constraints can be represented as structured fields or maintained rules.
The deterministic search shows source passages; it does not infer undocumented capabilities.
The seller enters customer responses through a short structured form; no recording or transcription is required.
The proposed renewal review is an ambition, not an existing customer service.
GDPR applies to account information and customer notes. Access planning includes consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Completeness and ownership of the service catalogue and delivery constraints.
Which promises require service-delivery or commercial approval.
How often requirements involve exceptions or bespoke services.
Whether customers would value a separate service-fit review.
Existing permissions and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which eligibility checks can be encoded without hiding important exceptions?
Can comparison drafts preserve limitations as reliably as benefits?
What minimum requirements make an initial feasibility brief useful to a sales engineer?
new_work: Maintain capability fields, exclusions and source versions.
Review comparisons for missing limitations and unsupported benefits.
Escalate uncertain feasibility to service specialists.
Evaluate whether proposed service-fit reviews improve customer decisions.

tasks.short: Give relevant promotional materials to people at meetings and events.

steps.what: Select current, approved promotional materials from the {DOCS}.
Coordinate quantities, printing and delivery with the marketing coordinator.
Check and pack printed materials for the event.
Offer attendees relevant materials and briefly explain their purpose.
Email requested digital materials to attendees who supplied their contact details.

tasks.design: Approved collections in the {DOCS} populate event packs, and a configured {WORKFLOW} sends internal preparation requests using agreed quantity rules. An attendee can request a specific digital item through a form, triggering its approved link through {EMAIL}. Packing, choosing what to offer and the event conversation remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task is mostly physical and interpersonal; small administrative savings rarely justified a separate build.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document collections, forms and notification rules can cover preparation and requested delivery with little custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Physical packing, event logistics and judging when an attendee welcomes an approach.
tasks.human_edge: Reading interest, choosing a relevant item and making a useful personal introduction.
tasks.altitude: Event days remain largely unchanged, with less coordination and follow-up email. No new decision rights are gained.

reach.task: Prepare audience-specific demonstration and information kits.
reach.learn: Approved service examples, accessible formats and matching materials to audience needs.

evidence.claim: Approved document collections, internal forms and requested-link delivery can be configured without a model.
Physical distribution and attendee interaction limit the overall time saving.
No digest case establishes a measured improvement for event-material distribution.

assumptions: Printed distribution remains useful; digital delivery is an attendee choice.
Preparation requests stay within preauthorised quantities and do not place supplier orders.
Approved materials have current versions and audience or language tags.
Automatic delivery sends only the item explicitly requested to the supplied address.
A material request does not enrol an attendee in broader marketing.
GDPR and applicable national marketing rules govern contact capture and retention. Access estimates include any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Whether events use printed materials, digital materials or both.
Who currently handles printing and physical preparation.
Existing document tags, approved collections and request forms.
Typical event volumes and administrative effort.
Applicable contact-retention rules and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can existing {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW} configuration cover the entire administrative portion?
Which materials do attendees request often enough to justify a dedicated digital collection?
new_work: Keep event collections and approved links current.
Handle incorrect addresses and failed deliveries.
Maintain quantity defaults and event preparation rules.
Remove expired contact requests according to retention rules.

role.altitude: The sales representative spends less time assembling prospect lists, finding contract facts and preparing comparisons. Discovery, recommendations and relationship conversations remain central; broader commercial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Sales manager: compare prospect cohorts and recommend territory priorities.
Sales engineer: prepare initial service-feasibility briefs.
Order clerk: verify that handover instructions match accepted terms.
Demonstrator and product promoter: assemble audience-specific information kits.
skills_to_grow: Maintain clear target criteria and interpret conversion evidence.
Check source-backed contract facts and capability claims.
Conduct discovery and explain service trade-offs.
Recognise feasibility exceptions and escalate them early.
Manage contact permissions and useful structured account records.
role.ambitious_version: A consultative seller who tests prospect cohorts frequently and offers documented service-fit reviews before renewal, supported by reliable account and capability information.

job.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel
